LESSON: WRITING 6.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: SPELLING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.5: Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why are some words commonly misspelt? 2. Why is it important to spell words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: Learner appropriately uses the target words in sentences of their own

• Digital literacy: Learner interacts with technology creating crossword puzzles and other word games and sharing them

through social media

• Learning to learn: Learner searches for the commonly misspelt or wrong articulation of signs of words from the internet thus

acquiring information on their own

Values:
Peace and unity are promoted as the learner takes part in group tasks

Link to other subjects

Correct spelling is emphasised in all other subjects such as Integrated Science, Kiswahili and Kenya Sign Language.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Adapted Course books, Recording devices e.g. tablets and mobile phones, Dictionary, Internet, Signed audio-visual recordings,
